A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FSP research. Their main text, appendices, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support reliable matching across renaming and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original path-star and sibling-discovery experiments, plus 3B/8B pretraining evaluations and ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original language-modeling evaluations, data-constrained pretraining studies, and attention analysis.

M1.justification: The single auxiliary head, bag-of-words BCE objective, reverse-LM summary targets, L2 alignment, and inference procedure remain unchanged. FSP-BCE becomes FSP-BoW; the newly documented architecture and teacher configuration do not establish a method change.

E1.justification: v2 adds held-out Dolci-Think and Dolmino evaluations of next-token predictive performance. The original synthetic tasks, reasoning/coding benchmarks, and pretraining sources remain. Reducing unique-token counts within the retained training coverage changes the protocol, not the domains.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain NTP, MTP, DS-MTP, MTP-Skip, and the existing auxiliary-head variants. New language-modeling and data-constrained comparisons reuse NTP/MTP/DS-MTP. Newly discussed methods such as Twin Networks and SemFormer are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v2 adds fixed training-token-budget studies: 8B training on 50B unique tokens for 20 epochs, and 3B training with 250B down to 5B unique tokens over increasing repetitions. It also adds NLL/NTA evaluation over approximately 4M held-out tokens and task-averaged scores. Existing benchmark protocols remain; ARC's accuracy-to-pass@1 wording is equivalent.

E4.justification: Existing head-count, summary-window, tf-idf, and teacher-layer analyses are retained. Figures 6 and 8 add substantial sensitivity studies of data availability and reuse. Figure 7 adds a final-layer attention analysis testing whether reverse-LM summaries preserve component structure in sibling discovery.

E5.justification: Existing seed counts and mean/standard-error reporting remain. However, new Tables 6–7 report three-seed means without standard errors, and the new data-constrained plots lack uncertainty bars. This introduces less complete uncertainty reporting for the added evidence; no increase in run counts is established.

E6.justification: v2 adds language-modeling results, data-reuse curves, and attention findings. In the new 8B 50B-token/20-epoch setting, Figure 6 reports average scores of 39.90% for FSP-RevLM, 37.84% for NTP, and 39.78% for MTP. Tables 1–3 and the relocated 3B ablation table retain their values. Table 4 changes MTP on G(2,8) from 0.49 to 0.48, and Figure 4 revises error-bar values.

T1.justification: The mathematical objectives and parameterizations in Equations 1–15 are retained. Neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs. Additional architectural formulas and explanations of prior methods do not introduce substantive theoretical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contributions: future-summary auxiliary supervision, handcrafted and reverse-LM variants, and improved reasoning/coding performance at 3B/8B scale. The added experiments support these claims without replacing or materially broadening them.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly discusses roughly doubled training compute and argues for its value under data constraints. It adds interpretations concerning overfitting under data reuse, structure preservation in reverse-LM attention, and possible post-training benefits from solution diversity. These substantially extend v1's explanations of long-horizon supervision and irrelevant future tokens.

D1.justification: Appendix D.1 and Table 5 newly specify the LLaMA-3-based architectures, widths/layers, attention configuration, RoPE, normalization, initialization, BF16, FSDP, AdamW, and warmup. Section 4.1 also discloses matching forward/reverse model sizes and training steps. These substantially expand v1's comparatively brief hardware and hyperparameter recipe.

R1.justification: Section 5 and new Appendix A substantially expand research positioning. They acknowledge Twin Networks as a close reverse-state-matching antecedent, discuss related unordered-future objectives from SemFormer and Frydenlund, and distinguish FSP's framework, diagnostic insights, and transformer-scale validation. Additional discussion covers latent prediction and data-constrained training.

P1.justification: The core exposition remains largely intact. Changes include consistent FSP-BoW terminology, affiliation/venue edits, expanded explanatory passages, merging former Section 4.3 into 4.2, and organizing the appendices into related work, MTP variants, synthetic experiments, and real-world pretraining with a contents page.

P2.justification: v2 adds data-constrained plots, attention heatmaps, an architecture table, and two language-modeling tables. Figures 1 and 3–5 are restyled, including revised labels, colors, sizing, and captions. The original 3B ablation table is retained as Table 8; Figure 6's standard-training panel aggregates existing Table 1 results.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important omissions through substantially fuller implementation details, explicit compute-cost discussion, recognition of close prior work, and new language-modeling/data-reuse evidence. These improve reproducibility and scientific positioning beyond the unchanged headline results. Reporting weaknesses remain: new results lack consistent uncertainty, and Figure 8's universal-superiority claim conflicts with Dolci-Think accuracy at 12.5B tokens. Those weaknesses limit the new conclusions but do not outweigh the substantial gains.
